claim: Genetic variation among orthologous proteins can cause cryptic phenotypic properties that only manifest in changing environments.
source: Genetic variation among orthologous proteins can cause cryptic phenotypic properties that only manifest in changing environments.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that introduces the concept of cryptic genetic variation.

claim: Cryptic genetic variation may impact the evolvability of proteins.
source: Such variation may impact the evolvability of proteins, but the underlying molecular basis remains unclear.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a motivation for the study.

claim: Four orthologous metallo-β-lactamases were subjected to comparative directed evolution toward a new function.
source: Here, we performed comparative directed evolution of four orthologous metallo-β-lactamases toward a new function and found that different starting genotypes evolved to distinct evolutionary outcomes.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach taken in the study.

claim: Different starting genotypes evolved to distinct evolutionary outcomes.
source: Here, we performed comparative directed evolution of four orthologous metallo-β-lactamases toward a new function and found that different starting genotypes evolved to distinct evolutionary outcomes.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the directed evolution experiments.

claim: One ortholog with low initial fitness reached a significantly higher fitness plateau than its counterparts via increasing catalytic activity.
source: Despite a low initial fitness, one ortholog reached a significantly higher fitness plateau than its counterparts, via increasing catalytic activity.
evidence: This describes a key result from the comparative evolution experiment.

claim: The ortholog with the highest initial activity evolved to a less-optimal and phenotypically distinct outcome through changes in expression, oligomerization and activity.
source: By contrast, the ortholog with the highest initial activity evolved to a less-optimal and phenotypically distinct outcome through changes in expression, oligomerization and activity.
evidence: This describes another key result contrasting with the first ortholog's evolution.

claim: Cryptic molecular properties and conformational variation of active site residues in the initial genotypes cause epistasis that could lead to distinct evolutionary outcomes.
source: We show how cryptic molecular properties and conformational variation of active site residues in the initial genotypes cause epistasis, that could lead to distinct evolutionary outcomes.
evidence: This is a mechanistic conclusion from the study based on structural and computational analyses.

claim: Cryptic genetic variation has been shown to play an important role in evolution because genetically diverse populations are more likely to contain genotypes with a 'pre-adapted' phenotype.
source: Cryptic genetic variation has been shown to play an important role in evolution because genetically diverse populations are more likely to contain genotypes with a 'pre-adapted' phenotype, for example, a latent promiscuous function, that may confer an immediate selective advantage when the environment changes and a new selection pressure emerges (Queitsch et al., 2002; Specchia et al., 2010; de Visser et al., 2011; Amitai et al., 2007; Bloom et al., 2007; Rohner et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: We have little understanding of how genetic variation affects the long-term adaptive evolutionary potential (or 'evolvability') of proteins.
source: Beyond that specific scenario, however, we have little understanding of how genetic variation affects the long-term adaptive evolutionary potential (or 'evolvability') of proteins (Wagner, 2008).
evidence: This identifies a knowledge gap that motivates the study.

claim: Many biological traits, in particular promiscuous protein functions, evolve by accumulating multiple adaptive mutations before reaching a fitness plateau or peak.
source: Many biological traits, in particular promiscuous protein functions, evolve by accumulating multiple adaptive mutations before reaching a fitness plateau or peak.
evidence: This is a general statement about protein evolution based on established knowledge.

claim: The degree to which a trait can improve and the level of fitness that it can reach ultimately determines the evolutionary potential and outcome of a given genotype.
source: Thus, the degree to which a trait can improve and the level of fitness that it can reach ultimately determines the evolutionary potential and outcome of a given genotype (Romero and Arnold, 2009).
evidence: This is a conceptual statement supported by citation.

claim: Intramolecular epistasis is prevalent and the phenotypic effect of the same mutation can be drastically altered when introduced into a genotype that differs by only a few other mutations.
source: Recent studies have shown that intramolecular epistasis is prevalent and that the phenotypic effect of the same mutation can be drastically altered when introduced into a genotype that differs by only a few other mutations, which may lead to different evolutionary outcomes depending on the starting genotype (Blount et al., 2008; de Visser and Krug, 2014; Parera and Martinez, 2014; Starr and Thornton, 2016; Miton and Tokuriki, 2016; Harms and Thornton, 2014; Starr et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior studies.

claim: Orthologous enzymes can exhibit a broad range of phenotypic responses to the same selection pressure to improve their promiscuous activity.
source: It has also been shown that orthologous enzymes can exhibit a broad range of phenotypic responses to the same selection pressure to improve their promiscuous activity (Khanal et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The degree to which genetic starting points determines long-term evolutionary outcomes under identical selection remains unclear.
source: These studies, however, have only focused on the effect of small mutational steps; the degree to which genetic starting points determines long-term evolutionary outcomes under identical selection remains unclear (O'Loughlin, 2006; Burch and Chao, 2000).
evidence: This identifies a knowledge gap in the field.

claim: Our understanding of the molecular mechanisms that underlie the relationship between genetic variation and evolvability is highly limited.
source: More importantly, our understanding of the molecular mechanisms that underlie the relationship between genetic variation and evolvability is highly limited.
evidence: This identifies a knowledge gap that the study aims to address.

claim: Protein fold and protein stability can shape evolvability, but these alone cannot explain the prevalence of epistasis and the enormous variation we observe in the evolvability of different genotypes.
source: It has been suggested that protein fold (Tóth-Petróczy and Tawfik, 2014; Yip and Matsumura, 2013; Schulenburg et al., 2015) and protein stability (Weinreich and Chao, 2005; Bloom and Arnold, 2009; Tokuriki and Tawfik, 2009) can shape evolvability, but these alone cannot explain the prevalence of epistasis and the enormous variation we observe in the evolvability of different genotypes.
evidence: This claim synthesizes prior work and identifies limitations in current understanding.

claim: Metallo-β-lactamases (MBLs) encompass a genetically diverse enzyme family that confer β-lactam antibiotic resistance to bacteria.
source: Metallo-β-lactamases (MBLs) encompass a genetically diverse enzyme family that confer β-lactam antibiotic resistance to bacteria (Figure 1A,B) (Meini et al., 2014; Bebrone, 2007).
evidence: This is a factual statement about MBLs supported by citations and referenced figures.

claim: Most MBLs exhibit phosphonate monoester hydrolase (PMH) activity (kcat/KM) in the range of 0.1 to 10 M−1s−1.
source: Our previous work demonstrated that most MBLs exhibit phosphonate monoester hydrolase (PMH) activity (kcat/KM) in the range of 0.1 to 10 M−1s−1 (Baier and Tokuriki, 2014; Baier et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' previous published work.

claim: β-lactam and phosphonate monoester hydrolyses differ in the cleaved bond (C-N vs. P-O) and the geometry of the transition state (tetrahedral vs. trigonal bipyramidal).
source: β-lactam and phosphonate monoester hydrolyses differ in the cleaved bond (C-N vs. P-O) and the geometry of the transition state (tetrahedral vs. trigonal bipyramidal), making the PMH activity a catalytically distinct promiscuous activity for these enzymes.
evidence: This is a chemical description of the two reactions.

claim: The evolution of MBLs toward PMH activity can be considered a model for neo-functionalization or the evolutionary emergence of a new enzyme function.
source: Thus, the evolution of MBLs toward PMH activity can be considered a model for neo-functionalization or the evolutionary emergence of a new enzyme function.
evidence: This is a conceptual framing of the experimental system based on the chemical differences between the two activities.

claim: Directed evolution was carried out with four different MBL orthologs: NDM1, VIM2, VIM7, and EBL1.
source: We performed directed evolution using four different MBL orthologs, New Delhi metallo- β-lactamase 1 (NDM1), Verona imipenemase 2 and 7 (VIM2 and VIM7), and Erythrobacter β-lactamase 1 (EBL1), as starting genotypes (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary file 1A).
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: VIM2 and NDM1 were chosen due to the availability of their biochemical and structural information.
source: VIM2 and NDM1 were chosen due to the availability of their biochemical and structural information (Garcia-Saez et al., 2008; King et al., 2012).
evidence: This explains the rationale for selecting these specific enzymes.

claim: VIM7 is a close homologous enzyme to VIM2 with 80% amino acid sequence identity.
source: VIM7 and EBL1 are close homologous enzymes to VIM2 (80% amino acid sequence identity) and NDM1 (55% amino acid sequence identity), respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the sequence relationship between the enzymes.

claim: EBL1 is a close homologous enzyme to NDM1 with 55% amino acid sequence identity.
source: VIM7 and EBL1 are close homologous enzymes to VIM2 (80% amino acid sequence identity) and NDM1 (55% amino acid sequence identity), respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the sequence relationship between the enzymes.

claim: The catalytic efficiencies for the native β-lactams hydrolysis are similar across the MBL enzymes (kcat/KM only varies up to twofold).
source: Although the catalytic efficiencies for the native β-lactams hydrolysis are similar across these enzymes (kcat/KM only varies up to twofold across all six MBLS), their kcat/KM for the promiscuous PMH activity varies by ~20 fold (Figure 1A and Supplementary file 1B).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of enzyme activities shown in the figure.

claim: The kcat/KM for the promiscuous PMH activity varies by ~20 fold across the MBL enzymes.
source: Although the catalytic efficiencies for the native β-lactams hydrolysis are similar across these enzymes (kcat/KM only varies up to twofold across all six MBLS), their kcat/KM for the promiscuous PMH activity varies by ~20 fold (Figure 1A and Supplementary file 1B).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of enzyme activities shown in the figure.

claim: PMH fitness in the directed evolution scheme is defined as the level of PMH activity in E. coli cell lysate.
source: Note that the 'PMH fitness' (i.e. the selection criteria) in our directed evolution scheme is defined as the level of PMH activity in E. coli cell lysate; as a result, PMH fitness is a function of catalytic activity and soluble expression levels in the cell.
evidence: This defines a key experimental parameter.

claim: PMH fitness is a function of catalytic activity and soluble expression levels in the cell.
source: Note that the 'PMH fitness' (i.e. the selection criteria) in our directed evolution scheme is defined as the level of PMH activity in E. coli cell lysate; as a result, PMH fitness is a function of catalytic activity and soluble expression levels in the cell.
evidence: This explains what factors contribute to the measured fitness.

claim: The PMH fitness differences between NDM1 and VIM2 wild-type originate from their kinetic parameters, while their solubility is comparable.
source: For example, the PMH fitness differences between NDM1 and VIM2 wild-type originate from their kinetic parameters, while their solubility is comparable (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This explains the molecular basis for fitness differences between two enzymes.

claim: EBL1 and VIM2 wild-type have similar catalytic efficiencies but their PMH fitness differ by 35-fold due to large differences in protein expression.
source: By contrast, EBL1 and VIM2 wild-type have similar catalytic efficiencies but their PMH fitness differ by 35-fold due to large differences in protein expression (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This explains the molecular basis for fitness differences between two other enzymes.

claim: Over the first two rounds of directed evolution (R2), significant differences in the extent of fitness improvement were observed among the four parallel trajectories.
source: Over the first two rounds of directed evolution (R2), we observed significant differences in the extent of fitness improvement among the four parallel trajectories (Figure 1D).
evidence: This describes an observation from the directed evolution experiment.

claim: Improvements in PMH fitness did not correlate with the initial fitness level.
source: Interestingly, improvements in PMH fitness did not correlate with the initial fitness level.
evidence: This is an observation from the directed evolution results.

claim: VIM2 exhibited only a 4-fold improvement in PMH fitness over the wild-type despite having the highest initial activity.
source: For example, although VIM2 is the variant with the highest initial activity, it only exhibited a 4-fold improvement in PMH fitness over the wild-type, and was surpassed by other, initially less fit variants such as NDM1 and EBL1, with a 210- and 310-fold improvement in PMH fitness, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the directed evolution experiment.

claim: NDM1 exhibited a 210-fold improvement in PMH fitness over the wild-type.
source: For example, although VIM2 is the variant with the highest initial activity, it only exhibited a 4-fold improvement in PMH fitness over the wild-type, and was surpassed by other, initially less fit variants such as NDM1 and EBL1, with a 210- and 310-fold improvement in PMH fitness, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the directed evolution experiment.

claim: EBL1 exhibited a 310-fold improvement in PMH fitness over the wild-type.
source: For example, although VIM2 is the variant with the highest initial activity, it only exhibited a 4-fold improvement in PMH fitness over the wild-type, and was surpassed by other, initially less fit variants such as NDM1 and EBL1, with a 210- and 310-fold improvement in PMH fitness, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the directed evolution experiment.

claim: The close pairs of homologues EBL1/NDM1 and VIM2/VIM7 follow similar trends in PMH fitness improvement.
source: Overall, the close pairs of homologues EBL1/NDM1 and VIM2/VIM7, seem to follow similar trends in PMH fitness improvement.
evidence: This is an observation about patterns in the evolution of related enzymes.

claim: Both NDM1 and VIM2 trajectories exhibited diminishing returns in their evolution toward a new activity, eventually reaching a plateau.
source: Overall, both trajectories exhibited diminishing returns in their evolution toward a new activity, that is each trajectory eventually reached a plateau where no substantial fitness increase was obtained in the last rounds of directed evolution.
evidence: This describes a general pattern observed in both evolutionary trajectories.

claim: In the last two rounds (R9 and R10), purifying selection was replaced by a pre-screening for increased PMH fitness on agar plates (>5000 variants), yet no variant with increased PMH fitness was isolated.
source: Note that in the last two rounds (R9 and R10), purifying selection was replaced by a pre-screening for increased PMH fitness (PMH activity level in the cell) on agar plates (>5000 variants), yet no variant with increased PMH fitness was isolated, suggesting that fitness plateaued in both trajectories (Figure 1D).
evidence: This describes a methodological change and its result.

claim: NDM1-WT was initially ~4 fold less-fit than VIM2-WT in PMH fitness.
source: Besides the similar overall trend along the trajectories, there are substantial differences in their evolutionary outcomes: while NDM1-WT was initially ~4 fold less-fit than VIM2-WT in PMH fitness, NDM1 fitness became ~28 fold higher than that of VIM2 by the end of the evolutionary experiment (R10).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of initial fitness levels.

claim: NDM1 fitness became ~28 fold higher than that of VIM2 by the end of the evolutionary experiment (R10).
source: Besides the similar overall trend along the trajectories, there are substantial differences in their evolutionary outcomes: while NDM1-WT was initially ~4 fold less-fit than VIM2-WT in PMH fitness, NDM1 fitness became ~28 fold higher than that of VIM2 by the end of the evolutionary experiment (R10).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of final fitness levels.

claim: The NDM1 trajectory displays a ~3600 fold increase in PMH fitness between NDM1-R10 and NDM1-WT.
source: Overall, the NDM1 trajectory displays a ~ 3600 fold increase in PMH fitness (between NDM1-R10 and NDM1-WT), whereas the VIM2 trajectory only exhibits a ~ 35 fold increase in PMH fitness (Figure 1D and Supplementary file 1G), resulting in over a 100-fold difference in PMH fitness improvement between the two trajectories.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the directed evolution experiment.

claim: The VIM2 trajectory exhibits a ~35 fold increase in PMH fitness.
source: Overall, the NDM1 trajectory displays a ~ 3600 fold increase in PMH fitness (between NDM1-R10 and NDM1-WT), whereas the VIM2 trajectory only exhibits a ~ 35 fold increase in PMH fitness (Figure 1D and Supplementary file 1G), resulting in over a 100-fold difference in PMH fitness improvement between the two trajectories.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the directed evolution experiment.

claim: There is over a 100-fold difference in PMH fitness improvement between the NDM1 and VIM2 trajectories.
source: Overall, the NDM1 trajectory displays a ~ 3600 fold increase in PMH fitness (between NDM1-R10 and NDM1-WT), whereas the VIM2 trajectory only exhibits a ~ 35 fold increase in PMH fitness (Figure 1D and Supplementary file 1G), resulting in over a 100-fold difference in PMH fitness improvement between the two trajectories.
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of the two evolutionary trajectories.

claim: The variation in evolutionary potential that separates NDM1 and VIM2 orthologous sequences is substantial, given that the two wild-type enzymes were almost identical in terms of their physicochemical properties, protein solubility, stability and structure.
source: Given that the two wild-type enzymes were almost identical in terms of their physicochemical properties, protein solubility, stability and structure (Figure 1A,B), the variation in evolutionary potential that separates these orthologous sequences is substantial.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results emphasizing the significance of the findings.

claim: NDM1 accumulated 13 mutations over the course of directed evolution.
source: Overall, NDM1 and VIM2 accumulated 13 and 15 mutations, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from sequencing the evolved variants.

claim: VIM2 accumulated 15 mutations over the course of directed evolution.
source: Overall, NDM1 and VIM2 accumulated 13 and 15 mutations, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from sequencing the evolved variants.

claim: The mutations that occurred along the NDM1 and VIM2 trajectories were entirely distinct.
source: Interestingly, the mutations that occurred along each trajectory were entirely distinct (Figure 1E and Supplementary file 1F).
evidence: This is an observation from comparing the sequences of evolved variants.

claim: Only two mutations occurred at the same position (154 and 223) in NDM1 and VIM2, and these were mutated to different amino acids.
source: Only two mutations occurred at the same position (154 and 223), and these were mutated to different amino acids.
evidence: This is an observation from comparing the sequences of evolved variants.

claim: The mutations in the early rounds of NDM1 evolution that conferred the largest PMH fitness improvements were W93G, N116T, and K211R.
source: For example, the mutations in the early rounds of evolution, which conferred the largest PMH fitness improvements, were W93G, N116T, and K211R in the NDM1 trajectory, and V72A, and F67L for VIM2.
evidence: This identifies specific mutations and their effects.

claim: The mutations in the early rounds of VIM2 evolution that conferred the largest PMH fitness improvements were V72A and F67L.
source: For example, the mutations in the early rounds of evolution, which conferred the largest PMH fitness improvements, were W93G, N116T, and K211R in the NDM1 trajectory, and V72A, and F67L for VIM2.
evidence: This identifies specific mutations and their effects.

claim: In NDM1, most mutations are scattered relatively evenly around the active site.
source: In NDM1, most mutations are scattered relatively evenly around the active site; only one mutation (W93G) is located below loop 3, and several are located in and around loop 10 and other parts of the active site.
evidence: This describes the spatial distribution of mutations based on structural analysis.

claim: In VIM2, six mutations are tightly clustered within or next to loop 3.
source: By contrast, in VIM2, six mutations are tightly clustered within or next to loop 3.
evidence: This describes the spatial distribution of mutations based on structural analysis.

claim: Distinct fitness outcomes result from distinct mutational responses in NDM1 and VIM2.
source: These results demonstrate that, for these two enzymes, distinct fitness outcomes result from distinct mutational responses.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation of different mutations in the two trajectories.

claim: Most positive variants isolated in the additional screening possess mutations at the same positions as previously identified in the original directed evolution.
source: Strikingly, most positive variants isolated in the additional screening possess mutations at the same positions as previously identified: Trp93 (in R1) and Met154 (R5) were isolated for NDM1. For VIM2, Val72 (R1), Phe67 (R2), Ser202 (R4), Thr263 (R5), and Val41 (R6) were isolated again (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary file 1H).
evidence: This is a result from replaying the first round of evolution with additional libraries.

claim: Only a handful of adaptive mutations, which are unique to each genotype, are available from the wild-type sequence.
source: These results suggest that only a handful of adaptive mutations, which are unique to each genotype, are available, at least from the wild-type sequence.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the repeated isolation of the same mutations.

claim: In the VIM2 trajectory, later mutations confer no differential fitness effect when directly introduced on the wild-type background.
source: In the VIM2 trajectory, we observed no differential fitness effect when later mutations are directly introduced on the wild-type background.
evidence: This is a result from epistasis analysis experiments.

claim: In NDM1, later mutations only confer a selective advantage if introduced after the initial fixation of R1 mutations.
source: On the contrary in NDM1, later mutations only confer a selective advantage if introduced after the initial fixation of R1 mutations (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a result from epistasis analysis experiments.

claim: W93G plays a permissive role for later mutations in NDM1, and the order of appearance of mutations in the NDM1 trajectory is rather constrained.
source: These results explain why only few mutations, for example W93G, were identified in the additional screening from the starting enzyme. This also suggests that W93G plays a permissive role for later mutations, and thus that the order of appearance of mutations in the NDM1 trajectory is rather constrained.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the epistasis analysis results.

claim: W93G increases PMH fitness in cell lysate by ~25 fold in NDM1-WT.
source: We found that each trajectory's adaptive mutations are incompatible with one another. While W93G increases PMH fitness in cell lysate by ~25 fold in NDM1-WT (104-fold with purified NDM1), it causes a 3-fold decrease in PMH fitness when introduced into VIM2-WT (10-fold with purified VIM2), explaining why VIM2 never acquired this mutation (Figure 2C,E and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from measuring the effect of W93G in different backgrounds.

claim: W93G causes a 3-fold decrease in PMH fitness when introduced into VIM2-WT.
source: We found that each trajectory's adaptive mutations are incompatible with one another. While W93G increases PMH fitness in cell lysate by ~25 fold in NDM1-WT (104-fold with purified NDM1), it causes a 3-fold decrease in PMH fitness when introduced into VIM2-WT (10-fold with purified VIM2), explaining why VIM2 never acquired this mutation (Figure 2C,E and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from measuring the effect of W93G in different backgrounds.

claim: W93G exhibits beneficial effects in MBL homologs other than VIM2 and VIM1.
source: W93G exhibits beneficial effects in MBL homologs other than VIM2 and VIM1, consistent with the observation that Trp93 was not only selected in the NDM1 trajectory, but also in two other evolutionary trajectories, EBL1 and VIM7's (W93L in EBL1 and W93G in VIM7, respectively, Supplementary file 1F).
evidence: This is an observation from testing W93G in multiple enzyme backgrounds.

claim: Introducing other hydrophobic residues (A, V, L and F) at position 93 in VIM2 had similar negative effects as W93G.
source: Moreover, introducing other hydrophobic residues (A, V, L and F) at position 93 in VIM2 had similar negative effects, indicating that mutating Trp93 is largely deleterious in VIM2 (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a result from systematic mutagenesis experiments.

claim: V72A improved the PMH fitness of VIM2 by ~2 fold.
source: Similarly, V72A, which improved the PMH fitness of VIM2 by ~2 fold (1.7-fold with purified enzyme), was largely neutral in NDM1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and Supplementary file 1I).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from measuring the effect of V72A.

claim: V72A was largely neutral in NDM1.
source: Similarly, V72A, which improved the PMH fitness of VIM2 by ~2 fold (1.7-fold with purified enzyme), was largely neutral in NDM1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and Supplementary file 1I).
evidence: This is a result from measuring the effect of V72A in NDM1.

claim: The conventional paradigm of protein evolution suggests that higher protein stability, or greater soluble and functional expression, promotes protein evolvability by buffering the destabilizing effect of function-altering mutations.
source: The conventional paradigm of protein evolution is dominated by the idea that higher protein stability, or greater soluble and functional expression, promotes protein evolvability, by buffering the destabilizing effect of function-altering mutations and allowing a greater number of adaptive mutations to accumulate (Bloom and Arnold, 2009; Weinreich and Chao, 2005; Tokuriki and Tawfik, 2009).
evidence: This describes an established model in the field supported by citations.

claim: The stability-evolvability model fails to predict the difference in evolvability between NDM1 and VIM2, because their relative stability and soluble expression are similar.
source: This model, however, fails to predict the difference in evolvability between NDM1 and VIM2, because their relative stability and soluble expression are similar (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a critical observation that challenges the conventional model.

claim: By R10, the catalytic efficiency of NDM1 was improved by more than 18,000-fold compared to the wild-type (kcat/KM from 0.32 to 5900 M−1s−1).
source: By R10, the catalytic efficiency of NDM1 was improved by more than 18,000-fold compared to the wild-type (kcat/KM from 0.32 to 5900 M−1s−1, Figure 3A,B and Supplementary file 2B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from kinetic measurements of purified enzymes.

claim: At R1 in NDM1, kcat/KM increased by ~300 fold while solubility decreased from 43% to 25%.
source: This significant improvement in catalytic efficiency, however, was offset by a loss of soluble expression at R1, where kcat/KM increased by ~300 fold, while the solubility decreased from 43% to 25% (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from measuring both activity and solubility.

claim: The level of soluble expression in NDM1 never recovered after R1, while kcat/KM gradually increased until reaching the plateau observed in R7.
source: The level of soluble expression never recovered, while kcat/KM gradually increased until reaching the plateau observed in R7.
evidence: This describes the trajectory of two molecular properties over the course of evolution.

claim: The catalytic efficiency of VIM2 stagnated at round 6, with only a ~25 fold increase in kcat/KM overall.
source: By contrast, the catalytic efficiency of VIM2 stagnated at round 6, with only a ~ 25 fold increase in kcat/KM overall (VIM2-R10 compared to the wild-type).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from kinetic measurements.

claim: The subsequent PMH fitness improvements in VIM2 resulted from increasing soluble expression, from 40% to 70%.
source: The subsequent PMH fitness improvements resulted from increasing soluble expression, from 40% to 70% (Figure 3).
evidence: This explains the molecular basis for fitness improvements in later rounds of VIM2 evolution.

claim: Changes in solubility are only weakly correlated to changes in Tm.
source: Changes in solubility are only weakly correlated to changes in Tm (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), indicating that other factors such as kinetic stability or protein folding affect the level of soluble protein expression more than thermostability (Bershtein et al., 2012; Wyganowski et al., 2013; Lim et al., 2016; Pey et al., 2011).
evidence: This is an observation from comparing solubility and melting temperature data.

claim: NDM1 retains the same monomeric quaternary structure along its trajectory to NDM1-R10.
source: NDM1 retains the same monomeric quaternary structure along its trajectory to NDM1-R10.
evidence: This is a result from size-exclusion chromatography experiments.

claim: The monomeric VIM2-WT evolved to exist in an equilibrium between monomer and dimer by VIM2-R10.
source: The monomeric VIM2-WT, however, evolved to exist in an equilibrium between monomer and dimer by VIM2-R10 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a result from size-exclusion chromatography experiments.

claim: The catalytic efficiency of the dimeric state of VIM2-R10 for PMH is eightfold lower compared to the monomeric state (kcat/KM = 510 and 60 M−1s−1 for the monomer vs. dimer, respectively).
source: The catalytic efficiency of the dimeric state for PMH is eightfold lower compared to the monomeric state (kcat/KM = 510 and 60 M−1s−1 for the monomer vs. dimer, respectively), indicating that the dimer formation may be associated with an overall increase in solubility, rather than catalytic efficiency along the VIM2 trajectory (Figure 3—figure supplement 2) (Bershtein et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from kinetic measurements of separated oligomeric states.

claim: NDM1 adapted exclusively by increasing catalytic efficiency while compromising its soluble expression.
source: Altogether, our results suggest that two distinct molecular mechanisms underlie the observed differences in evolutionary trajectories. NDM1 adapted exclusively by increasing catalytic efficiency while compromising its soluble expression while VIM2 evolved by increasing its expression, oligomerization and activity.
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the molecular characterization data.

claim: VIM2 evolved by increasing its expression, oligomerization and activity.
source: Altogether, our results suggest that two distinct molecular mechanisms underlie the observed differences in evolutionary trajectories. NDM1 adapted exclusively by increasing catalytic efficiency while compromising its soluble expression while VIM2 evolved by increasing its expression, oligomerization and activity.
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the molecular characterization data.

claim: Differences in protein stability or soluble expression in the initial genotypes cannot explain the differences in evolvability between NDM1 and VIM2.
source: Our observations also indicate that differences in protein stability or soluble expression in the initial genotypes cannot explain the differences in evolvability between the two enzymes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the properties of the wild-type enzymes and their evolutionary outcomes.

claim: VIM2 variants consistently exhibit higher stability and solubility throughout the trajectory, yet the improvements in kcat/KM and PMH fitness are far lower than that of NDM1.
source: VIM2 variants consistently exhibit higher stability and solubility throughout the trajectory, yet the improvements in kcat/KM and PMH fitness are far lower than that of NDM1.
evidence: This is an observation that challenges the conventional stability-evolvability model.

claim: When the enzymes are expressed at 37°C, NDM1 variants are significantly less fit because of their lower soluble expression, whereas VIM2 variants maintain similar PMH fitness levels.
source: Interestingly, the genetic differences in the evolutionary end points can create additional cryptic variation that becomes apparent when the environment is changed: when the enzymes are expressed at 37°C (rather that 30°C at which they evolved for higher PMH fitness) NDM1 variants are significantly less fit because of their lower soluble expression, whereas VIM2 variants maintain similar PMH fitness levels even at higher temperature (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a result from testing the evolved variants under different environmental conditions.

claim: W93G removes steric hindrance between the side chain of Trp93 and the substrate, and generates a complementary pocket for the phenyl group below loop 3.
source: First, W93G removes steric hindrance between the side chain of Trp93 and the substrate, and generates a complementary pocket for the phenyl group below loop 3 (Figure 4B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a structural interpretation from crystal structures and MD simulations.

claim: There is an inward displacement of loop 3 by ~6 Å in NDM1-R10, which allows for improved π-π stacking interactions between Phe70 and the p-nitrophenol-leaving group.
source: Second, there is an inward displacement of loop 3 (Trp93 is located near the base of this loop) by ~6 Å, which allows for improved π-π stacking interactions between Phe70 and the p-nitrophenol-leaving group (Figure 4C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a structural observation from comparing crystal structures.

claim: Loop 10 is repositioned via reorganization of the local hydrogen bonding network (largely by K211R and G222D) in NDM1-R10, allowing it to interact with the leaving group of the substrate.
source: Third, loop 10 is repositioned via reorganization of the local hydrogen bonding network (largely by K211R and G222D), allowing it to interact with the leaving group of the substrate (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a structural interpretation from crystal structures.

claim: VIM2-R10 dimer reveals an unprecedented structural rearrangement: a full half of the structure exhibits a symmetrical domain-swapping between the two subunits.
source: This dimer reveals an unprecedented structural rearrangement: a full half of the structure exhibits a symmetrical domain-swapping between the two subunits (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure of VIM2-R10.

claim: The major structural rearrangement occurring between VIM2-WT and VIM2-R10 involves the reorganization of loop 3 resulting in its disorder in VIM2-R10.
source: Besides domain swapping, the major structural rearrangement occurring between VIM2-WT and VIM2-R10 involves the reorganization of loop 3 resulting in its disorder in VIM2-R10, which is most likely caused by six mutations within and next to loop 3 (Figures 1E and 4D).
evidence: This is a structural observation from comparing crystal structures.

claim: In NDM1-W93G, W93G eliminates the steric hindrance with the substrate, and allows loop 3 to shift inward to promote complementary interactions with the substrate.
source: NDM1-W93G showed similar structural adaptations to NDM1-R10 (described above); W93G eliminates the steric hindrance with the substrate, and allows loop 3 to shift inward to promote complementary interactions with the substrate, without the rearrangement of loop 10, which presumably occurs later in evolution.
evidence: This is an interpretation from MD simulations.

claim: In VIM2-WT, Trp93 adopts a different orientation to avoid steric hindrance, which instead promotes complementary interactions with the phenyl ring of the substrate.
source: By contrast, in VIM2-WT, Trp93 adopts a different orientation to avoid steric hindrance, which instead promotes complementary interactions with the phenyl ring of the substrate.
evidence: This is an interpretation from MD simulations.

claim: W93G in VIM2 removes beneficial substrate-enzyme interactions, thus causing a deleterious effect on catalytic efficiency.
source: Consequently, W93G in VIM2 removes beneficial substrate-enzyme interactions, thus causing a deleterious effect on catalytic efficiency.
evidence: This is an interpretation from MD simulations that explains the experimental observations.

claim: In NDM1, Leu65, Gln123 and Asp124 constrain Trp93 to point toward the active site.
source: In NDM1, Leu65, Gln123 and Asp124 constrain Trp93 to point toward the active site (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a structural observation from crystal structures.

claim: In VIM2, the second shell residues (Gln65, Asp123, and Asp124) differ from NDM1, resulting in Trp93 being stabilized in an alternative conformation.
source: In VIM2, however, the second shell residues (Gln65, Asp123, and Asp124) differ, resulting in Trp93 being stabilized in an alternative conformation (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a structural observation from crystal structures.

claim: Remote and seemingly neutral sequence variation between the enzymes has substantial impact on the mutagenesis of a key active site residue.
source: Thus, remote and seemingly neutral sequence variation between the enzymes has substantial impact on the mutagenesis of a key active site residue.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the structural analysis of second-shell residues.

claim: The effects of W93G and V72A on both PMH and β-lactamase activities vary consistently and significantly across orthologous enzymes, even between orthologs with high sequence identity.
source: We found that their effects on both PMH and β-lactamase activities vary consistently and significantly, even between orthologs with high sequence identity (Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and Supplementary file 1I).
evidence: This is a result from systematic mutagenesis experiments across multiple enzymes.

claim: In VIM7, which is 80% identical to VIM2, W93G caused a ~3 fold increase in PMH activity, despite the same mutation causing an antagonistic 10-fold decrease in PMH activity in VIM2.
source: For example, in VIM7, which is 80% identical to VIM2, W93G caused a ~ 3 fold increase in PMH activity, despite the same mutation causing an antagonistic 10-fold decrease in PMH activity in VIM2.
evidence: This is a quantitative result demonstrating epistasis between closely related enzymes.

claim: Cryptic and subtle differences in sequence and structure in both orthologs may influence the conformation of Trp93, a key active site residue, and cause the observed 1000-fold difference in the phenotypic effect of mutation W93G.
source: Taken together, cryptic and subtle differences in sequence and structure in both orthologs may influence the conformation of Trp93, a key active site residue, and cause the observed 1000-fold difference in the phenotypic effect of mutation W93G (100-fold increase in NDM1 vs. 10-fold decrease in VIM2).
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation that synthesizes structural and functional data.

claim: The accessibility of adaptive mutations from each starting point, at least within one mutational step, seems to depend on the starting genotype.
source: Thus, as previously discussed, the accessibility of adaptive mutations from each starting point, at least within one mutational step, seems to depend on the starting genotype (Figure 2).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mutagenesis and epistasis experiments.

claim: Not all enzymes evolve to their fitness maximum.
source: Our observations highlight that not all enzymes evolve to their fitness maximum, and that seemingly innocuous genetic variation may result in significant consequences for a protein's ability to evolve a new function.
evidence: This is a general conclusion from the study.

claim: Seemingly innocuous genetic variation may result in significant consequences for a protein's ability to evolve a new function.
source: Our observations highlight that not all enzymes evolve to their fitness maximum, and that seemingly innocuous genetic variation may result in significant consequences for a protein's ability to evolve a new function.
evidence: This is a general conclusion from the study.

claim: The PMH activity in MBLs is not likely to have ever been selected for and can be considered as a truly non-physiological and serendipitous promiscuous function.
source: The PMH activity (breaking P-O bond) in MBLs is not likely to have ever been selected for; it can thus be considered as a truly non-physiological and serendipitous promiscuous function (Khersonsky and Tawfik, 2010; Babtie et al., 2010; Copley, 2015).
evidence: This is a characterization of the PMH activity supported by citations.

claim: The promiscuous PMH activity of MBLs can be considered a cryptic and hidden 'pre-adapted' property.
source: Thus, the promiscuous PMH activity of MBLs can be considered a cryptic and hidden 'pre-adapted' property.
evidence: This is a conceptual framing of the PMH activity.

claim: Genetic variation can alter the level of promiscuous activities in enzymes.
source: Genetic variation can alter the level of promiscuous activities in enzymes (de Visser et al., 2011; Bloom et al., 2007; Amitai et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a general statement supported by citations.

claim: In MBLs, the catalytic efficiencies for PMH hydrolysis differ by ~20 fold among orthologous enzymes, while the catalytic efficiencies for β-lactams hydrolysis only vary by twofold.
source: Indeed, in MBLs, the catalytic efficiencies for PMH hydrolysis differ by ~20 fold among orthologous enzymes, while the catalytic efficiencies for β-lactams hydrolysis only vary by twofold (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of activities across enzymes.

claim: The initial fitness and/or the catalytic efficiencies of enzymes do not necessarily provide a good indicator of their evolutionary outcome, and thus of their evolvability.
source: Importantly, the initial fitness and/or the catalytic efficiencies of enzymes do not necessarily provide a good indicator of their evolutionary outcome, and thus of their evolvability (Khanal et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study supported by citation to related work.

claim: Genetic variation can significantly alter the accessibility of adaptive mutations, and starting points with lower fitness may reach much higher evolutionary plateaus than starting points endowed with higher initial fitness.
source: Genetic variation can significantly alter the accessibility of adaptive mutations, and starting points with lower fitness may reach much higher evolutionary plateaus than starting points endowed with higher initial fitness.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study.

claim: Adaptive evolutionary potential can be truly 'cryptic' and only apparent after evolution happens.
source: Thus, adaptive evolutionary potential can be truly 'cryptic' and only apparent after evolution happens, further complicating the prediction of the most successful initial genotypes.
evidence: This is a conceptual conclusion from the study.

claim: Independent evolutionary trials from a single genotype often follow very similar genetic and thus phenotypic trajectories, suggesting that only a limited amount of beneficial mutations is available from any single genotypic starting point.
source: On one hand, examples from nature and the laboratory have shown that independent evolutionary trials from a single genotype often follow very similar genetic and thus phenotypic trajectories; suggesting that only a limited amount of beneficial mutations is available from any single genotypic starting point, and in those cases evolution is largely deterministic (Weinreich et al., 2006; Salverda et al., 2011; Lobkovsky and Koonin, 2012; Dickinson et al., 2013; Palmer et al., 2015; Kaltenbach et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a synthesis of prior work supported by multiple citations.

claim: The prevalence of epistasis causes distinct effects when some adaptive mutation(s) are introduced on the genetic background of otherwise phenotypically similar orthologs.
source: On the other hand, the prevalence of epistasis causes distinct effects when some adaptive mutation(s) are introduced on the genetic background of otherwise phenotypically similar orthologs (Khanal et al., 2015; Parera and Martinez, 2014; Harms and Thornton, 2014; Starr et al., 2017), suggesting that genetic variation epistatically 'restricts' and/or 'permits' the accessibility of certain adaptive mutations (Harms and Thornton, 2013; Kaltenbach and Tokuriki, 2014; Starr and Thornton, 2016).
evidence: This is a synthesis of prior work supported by multiple citations.

claim: The successful evolution of new protein functions may rely on genetic drift to explore the sequence space, thereby creating a diverse genotypic pool presenting multiple, differentially evolvable, genotypes from which an evolutionary trajectory may arise.
source: The successful evolution of new protein functions may therefore rely on genetic drift to explore the sequence space, thereby creating a diverse genotypic pool presenting multiple, differentially evolvable, genotypes from which an evolutionary trajectory may arise (Harms and Thornton, 2014).
evidence: This is a conceptual model supported by citation.

claim: Protein stability, or soluble and functional expression of proteins, is the dominant factor in determining evolvability according to the established and conventional paradigm of protein evolution.
source: The established and conventional paradigm of protein evolution suggests that protein stability, or soluble and functional expression of proteins, is the dominant factor in determining evolvability (Bloom and Arnold, 2009; Tokuriki and Tawfik, 2009; Weinreich and Chao, 2005).
evidence: This describes an established model in the field supported by citations.

claim: Neither protein stability nor protein fold can account for variation in evolutionary potential between the MBL enzymes toward PMH activity.
source: However, in our study, neither protein stability nor protein fold can account for variation in evolutionary potential between the MBL enzymes toward PMH activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study that challenges conventional models.

claim: Strong epistasis in protein function can be caused by subtle conformational changes through the accumulation of mutations.
source: Indeed, many examples demonstrated that strong epistasis in protein function can be caused by subtle conformational changes through the accumulation of mutations (Tomatis et al., 2008; Harms and Thornton, 2014; Dellus-Gur et al., 2015; Yang et al., 2016; Campbell et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a synthesis of prior work supported by multiple citations.

claim: An in-depth understanding of the molecular and evolutionary mechanisms underlying the optimization of enzymatic functions is essential to developing our ability to understand and predict the evolution of enzymes.
source: Thus, an in-depth understanding of the molecular and evolutionary mechanisms underlying the optimization of enzymatic functions, in particular of promiscuous activities, is essential to developing our ability to understand and predict the evolution of enzymes.
evidence: This is a concluding statement about the importance of the work.

claim: It may be effective to explore diverse initial genotypes and identify the most evolvable starting sequences to successfully obtain an optimized functional protein.
source: While much effort has been devoted to developing technologies for better library construction and high-throughput screening (Dalby, 2011; Davids et al., 2013; Goldsmith et al., 2017), our observations suggest that it may also be effective to explore diverse initial genotypes and identify the most evolvable starting sequences to successfully obtain an optimized functional protein (Lapidoth et al., 2018; Kiss et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a practical implication of the study for protein engineering.

claim: Predicting the evolvability of proteins remains a challenge that will require more in-depth biochemical and biophysical characterizations.
source: Yet, predicting the evolvability of proteins remains a challenge that will require more in-depth biochemical and biophysical characterizations in order to dissect the molecular mechanisms driving the evolution of protein function (Miton et al., 2018; Clifton et al., 2018; Kaltenbach et al., 2018).
evidence: This identifies a remaining challenge in the field.
